BGP, QoS & Capacity Planning — Technical
Specification (Rev 4.1)
Core Network Engineering — Internal Reference
1. Peering Overview
This document defines eBGP peering, QoS marking, and capacity planning parameters for AS-64500
edge routers across three regional edge sites: EDGE-1, EDGE-2, and EDGE-3. All sessions use
multihop TTL of 2 unless otherwise noted, and MD5 authentication is mandatory except for IX
route-server peers.
2. Peer Table
Peer Remote ASN Site Session Type Keepalive/Hold (s) Max Prefixes
UpstreamA AS-7018 EDGE-1 eBGP Transit 10 / 30 900,000
UpstreamB AS-3356 EDGE-1 eBGP Transit 10 / 30 950,000
UpstreamC AS-1299 EDGE-2 eBGP Transit 10 / 30 920,000
IX-PeerX AS-24482 EDGE-1 eBGP Peering (IX) 3 / 9 50,000
IX-PeerY AS-4788 EDGE-2 eBGP Peering (IX) 3 / 9 45,000
IX-PeerZ AS-9902 EDGE-3 eBGP Peering (IX) 3 / 9 38,000
CustomerZ AS-65010 EDGE-1 eBGP Customer 5 / 15 1,000
CustomerW AS-65022 EDGE-3 eBGP Customer 5 / 15 1,500
3. Sample Configuration — UpstreamA (EDGE-1)
router bgp 64500
neighbor 198.51.100.1 remote-as 7018
neighbor 198.51.100.1 timers 10 30
neighbor 198.51.100.1 maximum-prefix 900000 90
neighbor 198.51.100.1 route-map RM-UPA-IN in
!
route-map RM-UPA-IN permit 10
set local-preference 150
set community 64500:100 additive
4. Sample Configuration — UpstreamC (EDGE-2)
router bgp 64500
neighbor 198.51.100.5 remote-as 1299
neighbor 198.51.100.5 timers 10 30
neighbor 198.51.100.5 maximum-prefix 920000 90
neighbor 198.51.100.5 route-map RM-UPC-IN in
!
route-map RM-UPC-IN permit 10
set local-preference 130
set community 64500:100 additive

5. QoS Marking Policy
Traffic is classified into three QoS classes at ingress based on DSCP marking: Voice (EF, DSCP 46)
receives strict-priority queuing up to 10% of interface bandwidth; Business-Critical (AF31, DSCP 26)
receives guaranteed minimum bandwidth of 30% with the ability to burst higher when capacity allows;
Best-Effort (DSCP 0) receives the remaining bandwidth with no guarantee and is the first class dropped
under congestion. Any traffic arriving without a recognized DSCP marking is treated as Best-Effort by
default, not as an error condition.
6. Community Tag Policy
Routes from customers are tagged 64500:200 and advertised to all upstreams and IX peers. Routes
from IX peers are tagged 64500:300 and are advertised only to customers, never to upstreams or other
IX peers. Routes from upstreams are tagged 64500:100 and are customer-facing only, never
re-advertised to upstreams or IX peers. If a route matches more than one condition, the more restrictive
tag takes precedence, where restrictiveness ranks IX (300) as most restrictive, followed by upstream
(100), followed by customer (200) as least restrictive.
7. Capacity Planning Formulas
Required uplink capacity: Required_Mbps = (Peak_Concurrent_Users × Avg_Session_Kbps) /
1000 × Overprovision_Factor. Standard Overprovision_Factor is 1.4. Avg_Session_Kbps is currently
220 Kbps per user, measured quarterly.
Redundancy headroom: Headroom_Percent = ((Current_Uplink_Mbps - Required_Mbps) /
Current_Uplink_Mbps) × 100. Sites with Headroom_Percent below 15% are flagged for capacity
upgrade planning in the following quarter.
8. Site Capacity Table
Site Peak Concurrent Users Current Uplink (Gbps)
EDGE-1 26,000 10
EDGE-2 31,000 10
EDGE-3 14,500 5
